projects.name: Trackr – Personal Finance App

projects.tldr:
• Designed and developed Trackr, a modern cross-platform personal finance app built with Flutter.

projects.summary:
Trackr is a mobile-first personal finance app that helps users master their finances through smart budgeting, advanced analytics, and seamless cloud sync. Built using Flutter and Firebase, it offers a refined, privacy-respecting alternative to traditional finance apps.

Trackr includes intelligent features like OCR receipt scanning, financial goal tracking, and a clean Material 3 UI with dark mode. Offline-first architecture ensures uninterrupted access to finances, while real-time sync keeps data consistent across devices.

The product is currently under final development for commercial release, focused on delivering delightful, secure, and intuitive financial management for individuals worldwide.

projects.name: ICU Mortality Modeling
projects.title: ML/Data Science Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Predicted ICU patient mortality using MIMIC-III clinical data and advanced machine learning models.
  • Preprocessed 37,000+ patient records with 7,000+ features: one-hot encoding, z-score standardisation, and comorbidity encoding via ICD-9 codes.
  • Addressed class imbalance with oversampling and validated performance using AUC-ROC on multiple models.
  • Compared logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, and deep neural networks (AUC up to 0.950).
  • Visualised data with UMAP and histograms; final model insights and comparisons available on the demo page.
projects.summary:
This project tackles the task of predicting in-hospital mortality using the MIMIC-III dataset, a rich collection of de-identified ICU patient records. The goal was to model the HOSPITAL_EXPIRE_FLAG using features collected at ICU admission, such as demographics, vitals, diagnostic codes, and comorbidities.

After merging and cleaning the dataset, over 7,000 features were engineered, including comorbidity information from secondary ICD-9 codes. Categorical features were one-hot encoded, and numerical features were standardised. To address strong class imbalance, the deceased class was oversampled. Feature distribution visualisations and UMAP projections revealed structural differences between outcome classes.

Multiple models were implemented and tuned, including logistic regression, regularised trees, random forests, boosted trees, and neural networks. The deep learning model achieved the highest out-of-sample AUC-ROC of 0.950, outperforming all others. The results highlight the value of ensemble and deep learning approaches when dealing with high-dimensional clinical data.

projects.name: Finance vs Birdsong: Time Series Classification
projects.title: ML/Data Science Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Developed and compared machine learning models to classify financial vs birdsong time series using extracted statistical features.
  • Implemented linear and tree-based classifiers with hyperparameter tuning and ROC-based model evaluation using R's tidymodels framework.
  • Visualized feature distributions, decision boundaries, ROC curves, and feature importance to interpret model performance.
  • Provided insights into key distinguishing features and model misclassification patterns.
  • Explore the full interactive analysis in the demo page.
projects.summary:
This project builds and evaluates multiple classification models to distinguish between financial and birdsong time series data based on extracted features such as linearity, entropy, and autocorrelation. Using the tidymodels framework in R, various classifiers including LDA, logistic regression, decision trees, random forest, and boosted trees were trained and tuned with cross-validation.

Model performance was assessed via accuracy metrics, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. Feature importance charts and decision boundary visualizations provided interpretability and insight into what drives classification differences.

This analysis aids understanding of how financial and audio time series differ statistically and how models can leverage these differences for accurate classification.

projects.name: Retail Forecasting: NT Electronics Turnover
projects.title: Data Scienctist
projects.tldr:
• Forecasted monthly turnover for Northern Territory’s electrical & electronic goods retail sector using classical time series methods.
  • Applied STL decomposition, Box-Cox transformations, and unit root tests to prepare the data.
  • Built, validated, and compared ETS and ARIMA models based on AIC and out-of-sample accuracy.
  • Assessed forecasts using residual diagnostics and updated real ABS data through to December 2024.
  • Interactive results and visualisations available on the demo page.
projects.summary:
This project builds ETS and ARIMA models to forecast monthly turnover in the Northern Territory’s electronics retail industry using data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (1998–2022). The series is transformed and decomposed using STL, with stationarity tested and differencing applied where appropriate.

Model performance is compared through AIC and test-set validation using the last 24 months of data. Residual diagnostics (ACF plots, Ljung-Box test) support model assumptions, while forecasts are validated against new ABS updates through 2024.

The analysis is fully reproducible and highlights the balance between model interpretability and forecast accuracy in retail economics.

projects.name: Cricket Performance PCA Analysis
projects.title: ML/Data Science Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Performed Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on women’s T20 cricket statistics to identify key performance dimensions in batting and bowling.
  • Reduced 19 performance metrics to 4 principal components explaining 84% of variance, revealing insights about player roles and skill levels.
  • Used bootstrap resampling and permutation testing to validate the robustness and significance of findings.
  • Visualized data clusters and player performance patterns with biplots, enabling nuanced understanding of player strengths.
  • For more details and interactive demo, visit the project page.
projects.summary:
This project applies Principal Component Analysis to a rich dataset of women's T20 cricket statistics to uncover the underlying structure of player performance metrics. By focusing on 19 numerical variables related to batting and bowling, the PCA reduces dimensionality to four key components that explain 84% of the variance. The components represent overall all-round performance, bowling volume, bowling quality, and standout individual achievements.

Robustness of the PCA results was assessed through bootstrap resampling, providing confidence intervals for the contributions of each metric. Permutation testing was used to validate correlations between key performance variables. Visual biplots help illustrate relationships and clusters among performance metrics and player profiles.

This analysis offers actionable insights for cricket statisticians and enthusiasts interested in advanced performance evaluation techniques.

projects.name: Teleoperation of Kuka Robotic Arm
projects.title: Software Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Led a team of three in developing a VR system for teleoperating a KUKA robotic arm with hand-tracking and a two-finger haptic feedback glove, improving user control and precision.
  • Designed, manufactured and tested the haptic glove, developed electrical schematics, and wrote Python scripts for two-way communication with the robotic arm.
  • Developed software for real-time robotic arm control, integrating the Robotiq Gripper 2F-140, Unity-based control system, and OPC UA communication.
  • Sourced and implemented cameras (Zed, RealSense, and LogiCamera) to enhance immersive teleoperation with a Xavier Jetson.
  • Led project administration, including team formation, ethics approval, risk assessments, and project planning.
projects.summary:
I led a team of three in developing an integrated virtual reality system designed to enhance user control and precision in teleoperating robotic arms. This system, implemented in the Monash Smart Manufacturing Hub's Digital Twin Lab, enables intuitive real-time manipulation of a KUKA robotic arm using VR hand-tracking and an advanced two-finger haptic feedback glove. Working every day for three months over the summer, we achieved significant milestones.

Haptic Glove

I designed and tested seven iterations of the glove, sourced components, created the electrical schematic, soldered and crimped connections, and wrote Python scripts on a Raspberry Pi Model 4B to enable two-way communication with the robotic arm gripper. Additionally, I designed the housing for the Raspberry Pi. The haptic glove now functions seamlessly upon power-up.



Robotic Arm

I wrote the KUKA Sunrise Java code that allows the robotic arm and end effector to receive values from the server, enabling real-time control. This required an in-depth understanding of OPC UA to create new variables, as well as extensive research into KUKA Sunrise and Robotiq Gripper 2F-140 documentation. Ultimately, I successfully integrated the gripper with both the KUKA robotic arm and the server.

VR & Hand Tracking

I developed the virtual lab environment that users interact with in VR. Additionally, I wrote C# scripts that track the user's hand, calculate movement differences, and transmit the data to the server for the robotic arm to mimic. I also wrote scripts for mapping gripper movement in Unity and learned how to integrate different robotic frames. Furthermore, I co-wrote the locomotion scripts that allow users to navigate the lab and authored the view-changer script, which lets users switch between different perspectives.



Camera Streams

I sourced and implemented a Zed Camera, RealSense Camera, and LogiCamera, integrating them with a Xavier Jetson to enhance teleoperation by making control more immersive and intuitive.



Software Development

My contributions extended to software development, where I wrote the code that connects the KUKA robotic arm to the server, implemented OPC UA for industrial communication, and developed the Unity-based control system for the gripper. Additionally, I engineered the hand-tracking system, calculated movement differences, and transmitted them to the server while integrating all camera streams for a seamless operator experience.

Administration

I formed and led the team, holding weekly meetings with our supervisor and bi-weekly meetings with the team. I also wrote all the necessary documentation to obtain ethics approval, including the Explanatory Statement, Consent Form, Interview Topics, and Survey Questions - ensuring we could conduct testing with participants. Additionally, I authored and secured approval for two detailed risk assessments, one for the project as a whole and another specifically for the full-body haptic suit, assuming the role of Risk Owner. I conducted extensive academic research in this field, developed a six-month project timeline (Gantt Chart), and contributed significantly to the project report.



Ultimately, this project was highly rewarding. By reducing cognitive strain and improving operational accuracy, we laid the groundwork for future advancements in haptic-enhanced teleoperation.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving
projects.title: ML Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Developed an autonomous delivery robot capable of navigating both urban and rural Australian roads using deep learning for real-time steering commands, and secured 1st place in the Need4Speed Challenge at RVSS 2025.
  • Collected and labeled 3,000 images to train the model, applying various data augmentation techniques for improved robustness.
  • Trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict seven distinct steering commands with ~75% accuracy, and incorporated stop sign detection using color thresholding.
  • Implemented dynamic speed control based on road conditions, ensuring optimal performance in both straight and curved roads.
  • For more information, visit the GitHub page.
projects.summary: I developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict vehicle steering for autonomous driving, enabling my robot to navigate both urban and rural roads. The model processed RGB camera images to generate real-time steering commands, incorporated stop sign detection, and dynamically adjusted speed based on road conditions. After extensive data collection, training, and deployment on a Raspberry Pi-controlled robot, I secured 1st place in the Need4Speed Challenge at RVSS 2025, demonstrating exceptional performance in autonomous navigation and real-world adaptability.

projects.name: Olympics Database
projects.title: Data Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Designed and implemented a comprehensive database system for PAT (Paris Arrow Transit), managing transportation logistics for official events like the Olympics.
  • Integrated relational and non-relational databases (SQL & MongoDB) for managing vehicle, driver, official, and trip details, ensuring smooth operation.
  • Created and modified the database, implementing business rules, triggers, and stored procedures for data integrity, including a trigger to suspend drivers based on demerit points.
  • For more information, visit the GitHub page.
projects.summary: I developed a robust database system for Paris Arrow Transit (PAT) to manage transportation logistics for events like the Olympics. I worked across both relational and non-relational databases, leveraging SQL, PL/SQL, and MongoDB to build a flexible and efficient system. My work involved not only creating and populating the database to meet specified requirements but also implementing advanced features such as sequence management and data integrity enforcement through triggers and stored procedures. I restructured the schema to accommodate new business rules, including managing official roles and handling complaints about drivers' behavior. The system was designed to automatically suspend drivers based on accumulated demerit points and ensure that all trip-related data adhered to business logic. Additionally, I integrated MongoDB to handle driver-trip data in JSON format, adding another layer of scalability to the project. Throughout, I ensured that the database was efficient, scalable, and aligned with future needs.

projects.title: Game Developer
projects.tldr:
• Developed an interactive space waste management game to raise awareness about environmental issues in space through engaging gameplay.
  • Designed and implemented spaceship controls and laser mechanics, creating a progressively challenging experience with increasing debris speed and quantity.
projects.summary:
I created an interactive game designed to simulate space waste management, raising awareness about environmental issues related to human waste in space. This project aimed to engage users in a fun way while educating them on the importance of proper space waste management.

The game works by having the user control a spaceship, moving it left and right using the arrow keys, and shooting lasers to destroy incoming space debris with the space bar. As the user progresses, the debris moves faster and in greater quantities. They earn points for every piece of debris destroyed.
